summary: Develop impact tolerances, scenario tests, crisis plans, and resilience dashboards in practical operational resilience training. Enquire today.
lede: Operational resilience frameworks training for financial services and critical infrastructure connects important business services to the processes, people, facilities, applications, data, suppliers, and utilities they depend on. You will learn to identify single points of failure, set impact tolerances, assess service criticality, and make recovery decisions that keep disruption within acceptable limits. Using ISO 22301 and ISO 31000 as reference points, the course provides practical experience with business impact analysis, dependency mapping, recovery measures such as RTO and RPO, scenario testing, crisis escalation, and resilience reporting. You will develop work products including a services register, dependency map, impact tolerance statement, scenario test pack, resilience risk register, and executive dashboard.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who protect critical services, coordinate disruption response, and report resilience exposure to executives, boards, auditors, regulators, and public-sector stakeholders. It suits experienced continuity and risk practitioners as well as adjacent technology and operations professionals who need a structured operational resilience approach.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to business continuity, operational risk, crisis management, enterprise risk, technology operations, or critical infrastructure services. Prior knowledge of ISO 22301 or ISO 31000 is helpful but not required. No coding or programming is required. You will use structured templates and spreadsheet or dashboard exercises rather than develop software. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted scenario analysis and automated resilience monitoring receive operational application treatment, not technical engineering or production deployment.
